    ABBREVIATED APPLICATION OF EASTERN SHORE NATURAL GAS COMPANY
                FOR CERTIFICATE OF PUBLIC CONVENIENCE
                            AND NECESSITY


           Pursuant to Sections 7(b) and 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act (“NGA”), as amended, 1 and Part

157 of the regulations of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“Commission” or

“FERC”), 2 Eastern Shore Natural Gas Company (“Eastern Shore”) hereby submits this

Application requesting authorization to construct, replace, and abandon facilities as part of the

Delmar Regional Enhancement Project (“Project”). The Project consists of five pipeline loop

segments, associated aboveground valve facilities, and the construction of a new meter and

regulator station designed to provide 15,800 dekatherms per day (“Dth/d”) of firm transportation

capacity on Eastern Shore’s existing interstate natural gas pipeline system in Pennsylvania,

Delaware, and Maryland. The Project cost is estimated at approximately $75,130,000. 3

           To meet the confirmed need of Eastern Shore’s shippers for additional firm natural gas

transportation capacity, Eastern Shore respectfully requests that the Commission issue an order

authorizing the Project by September 30, 2027.

 I.         DESCRIPTION OF EASTERN SHORE

           The exact legal name of Applicant is Eastern Shore Natural Gas Company. Eastern Shore

is a corporation organized and existing under the laws of the state of Delaware, with its principal

place of business located at 500 Energy Lane, Suite 200, Dover, Delaware 19901. Eastern Shore

is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Chesapeake Utilities Corporation (“Chesapeake”).

           Eastern Shore is a “natural-gas company” within the meaning of the NGA and operates in

the commonwealth of Pennsylvania and in the states of Delaware and Maryland as an open access

pipeline transporting natural gas in accordance with a blanket transportation certificate issued

under Part 284 of the Commission’s Regulations. 4 Eastern Shore also transports natural gas and

provides storage service in accordance with certain certificates of public convenience and

necessity issued by the Commission pursuant to Section 7(c) of the NGA and pursuant to Eastern

Shore’s FERC Gas Tariff (“Tariff”).

 III.   REGULATORY AUTHORIZATIONS REQUESTED

       Eastern Shore is seeking (1) authorization pursuant to Section 7(c) of the NGA and Part

157 of the Commission’s regulations to construct, own, operate, and maintain the Project facilities

and (2) authorization pursuant to Section 7(b) of the NGA to abandon certain facilities that have

been previously certificated by the Commission. Specifically, pursuant to Section 7(c) of the

NGA, Eastern Shore proposes to construct the following facilities:

•      Pennsylvania

       •       Parkesburg-Daleville Loop: Construct 2.55 miles of new 24-inch-diameter
               natural gas pipeline loop collocated within Eastern Shore’s existing pipeline
               corridor in Chester County, Pennsylvania.

       •       Gum Tree Rd RMV Station: Construct a new valve station in Chester County,
               Pennsylvania consisting of two remote monitoring valves, an in-line inspection
               facility, and a natural gas-powered generator.

       •       Daleville Compressor Station RMV: Construct a new remote monitoring valve
               and in-line inspection facility at the existing Daleville Compressor Station in
               Chester County, Pennsylvania.

•      Delaware

       •       Tidewater Upgrade Segment 1: Replace 0.32 miles of existing 6-inch-diameter
               natural gas pipeline with 16-inch diameter pipeline in New Castle County,
               Delaware.

       •       Tidewater Upgrade Segment 2: Replace 1.28 miles of existing 6-inch-diameter
               natural gas pipeline with 16-inch diameter pipeline in New Castle County,
               Delaware.

       •       Delaware City Compressor Station Valve: Construct a new manual shutoff valve
               within the fenceline of the existing Delaware City Compressor Station in New
               Castle County, Delaware.

       •       Harrington Loop: Construct 5.05 miles of new 16-inch-diameter natural gas
               pipeline loop in Kent County, Delaware.

       •       Harrington Loop RMV Station: Construct a new valve station in Kent County,
               Delaware consisting of one new remote monitoring valve, an in-line inspection
               facility, and a natural gas-powered generator.
        •       North Bridgeville M&R Station: Construct a new meter and regulator station on
               existing Eastern Shore-owned property adjacent to the fenced Bridgeville
               Compressor Station facility in Sussex County, Delaware.

       •       Felton Loop South RMV Station Modifications: Make minor modifications to
               the existing Felton Loop South RMV Station in Kent County, Delaware to tie-in
               the new Harrington Loop.

•      Maryland

       •       Barksdale Loop: Construct 1.85 miles of new 24-inch-diameter natural gas
               pipeline loop in Cecil County, Maryland.

       •       Telegraph Road RMV Station: Construct a new valve station in Cecil County,
               Maryland consisting of one new remote monitoring valve and a natural gas-
               powered generator.

       •       Barksdale Road RMV Station: Construct a new valve station in Cecil County,
               Maryland consisting of one new remote monitoring valve, an in-line inspection
               facility, and a natural gas-powered generator.

In addition, Eastern Shore requests abandonment authority pursuant to Section 7(b) of the NGA

for the following existing Eastern Shore facilities:

•      Pennsylvania

       •       Daleville Piping: Abandon the existing connection between the Daleville M&R
               Station and the 8-inch Parkesburg Line and reconfigure belowground station piping
               at the Daleville Compressor Station in Chester County, Pennsylvania.

•      Delaware

       •       Tidewater 6-Inch Line: Abandon approximately two miles of the existing 6-inch
               Tidewater Line in New Castle County, Delaware. Abandonment activities will also
               include miscellaneous reconfiguration between the abandoned and the existing
               pipeline facilities.

       •       North Bridgeville M&R Station: Abandon the existing North Bridgeville M&R
               station in Sussex County, Delaware.

•      Maryland

       •       Telegraph Road RMV Station: Abandon approximately 120 feet of belowground
               interconnect piping at the proposed Telegraph Rd RMV Station in Cecil County,
               Maryland.
 IV.     PROJECT PURPOSE AND MARKET SUPPORT

        The purpose of the Project is to provide the incremental firm transportation capacity

necessary to support demand growth for the participating shippers, two local distribution

companies serving human needs customers, including residential, hospital, and emergency

services customers, in Delaware and Maryland. Demand within the shippers’ service territories

has grown beyond the firm capacity currently available on Eastern Shore’s existing pipeline

system, and the Project is needed to allow the shippers to connect new customers and to continue

serving existing customers reliably under peak demand conditions.

        Eastern Shore held an open season from January 22, 2024 through February 23, 2024.

Following the open season, Eastern Shore entered into binding precedent agreements with two

current shippers for 20-year terms at negotiated rates for the full 15,800 Dth/d Project capacity:

Easton Utilities Commission (“Easton”) for 600 Dth/d and Eastern Shore’s affiliate Chesapeake

Utilities Corporation – Delaware Division (“CUC – Delaware”) for 15,200 Dth/d. Copies of the

precedent agreements with the Project shippers are included herewith as Exhibit I. 7

V.      CERTIFICATE POLICY STATEMENT AND PUBLIC CONVENIENCE AND
        NECESSITY

        The Commission’s Certificate Policy Statement establishes criteria for determining

whether there is a need for a proposed project and whether the proposed project will serve the

public interest. 8 The “threshold requirement for pipelines proposing new projects is that the

applicant must be prepared to financially support the project without relying on subsidization from

to eliminate or minimize any adverse effects the project might have on the applicant’s existing

groups are identified after efforts have been made to minimize them, the Commission will evaluate

the Project meets the Commission’s Certificate Policy Statement criteria and should be approved

as consistent with the public convenience and necessity.

            Subsidization And Impacts On Existing Customers

            As noted above, Eastern Shore has entered into long-term precedent agreements with two

current customers for the 15,800 Dth/d Project capacity at negotiated rates. Upon approval of the

Project, Eastern Shore and the shippers will enter into firm transportation agreements at negotiated

rates for the subscribed capacity. The amount of capacity subscribed represents 100 percent of the

proposed incremental capacity for the Project. Accordingly, the Project is not subsidized by

existing customers and is financially viable. Eastern Shore is the only interstate natural gas

pipeline serving the Delmarva Peninsula, and none of the facilities proposed would infringe on an

existing market area not currently served by Eastern Shore. Therefore, the Project will have no

adverse or competitive impact on existing pipelines and their captive customers.

        Impacts On Landowners And Communities

       Eastern Shore has designed the Project to minimize impacts to landowners and

communities by making maximum use of its existing pipeline system and siting the proposed

facilities within or adjacent to existing utility corridors and rights-of-way to the extent practicable.

As described in Section VII and the Environmental Report, the pipeline loop segments are

collocated within Eastern Shore’s existing pipeline corridor, and the associated aboveground

facilities are sited on or immediately adjacent to existing Eastern Shore-owned property,

substantially reducing the need for new land disturbance and new permanent easements. Eastern

Shore implemented a comprehensive outreach campaign to inform landowners and stakeholders

about the Project, solicit feedback, and provide multiple avenues for engagement. Eastern Shore

has developed a Public Outreach Plan, included with Resource Report 1 in the attached

Environmental Report, which describes the outreach activities undertaken and planned in

connection with the Project.

       Eastern Shore's outreach efforts began in late 2025, when Eastern Shore sent letters to

federal, state, and local permitting agencies, notifying them of the Project and its potential effects

on environmental resources within their respective jurisdictions. In July 2026, Eastern Shore

mailed a Project introduction letter to landowners and stakeholders in the Project area, describing

the proposed facilities, the anticipated construction timeline, and providing contact information

for questions and concerns. To ensure ongoing accessibility, Eastern Shore has established a

Project-specific website, a dedicated email address (delmarregionalenhancement@esng.com), and

a toll-free telephone number (1-844-366-3764) to enable interested parties to obtain additional

Project information, ask questions, and submit comments. This contact information is printed on
 all Project materials and included on the Project website, providing a single, centralized point of

contact for all inquiries.

        Eastern Shore will hold three in-person open houses in the Project area in November 2026

to provide local landowners and stakeholders with the opportunity to engage directly with Eastern

Shore’s Project team, review Project maps and materials, and ask questions about the proposed

facilities, construction activities, and easement acquisition process. Letters inviting stakeholders

and landowners to these open houses will be sent in October 2026. Eastern Shore is committed to

maintaining open lines of communication with affected landowners and stakeholders throughout

the permitting, construction, and restoration phases of the Project and will continue to respond to

inquiries and address concerns as they arise.

        With respect to land acquisition, Eastern Shore will seek to acquire all necessary easements

and rights-of-way through good-faith negotiations with affected landowners. Eastern Shore is

committed to working collaboratively with landowners to address site-specific concerns and,

where feasible, to adjust construction methods or workspace configurations to accommodate

landowner preferences and minimize disruption to ongoing land uses.

        Eastern Shore has been and will continue to be responsive to landowner and stakeholder

feedback received through its outreach efforts. Where practicable, Eastern Shore has incorporated

feedback into the Project design, including route refinements and adjustments to construction

workspaces to avoid or minimize impacts to residences, agricultural operations, and other sensitive

land uses. Eastern Shore will continue to evaluate and address concerns raised by landowners and

stakeholders throughout all phases of the Project.
            Project Overview – Mailed to Landowners and Stakeholders in July 2026



       Public Benefits

       Eastern Shore has been reliably serving the Delmarva Peninsula for more than 65 years as

the sole interstate natural gas pipeline in the region. As the demand for natural gas has continued

to increase across the Delmarva Peninsula, Eastern Shore has evaluated system enhancement
 projects to meet the growing needs of its customers and their end-use consumers. The Project will

provide 15,800 Dth/d of critically needed incremental firm transportation capacity on Eastern

Shore’s existing system, directly supporting the ability of local distribution companies to connect

new customers and to continue serving existing customers reliably, including during peak demand

conditions.

       In response to the open season, two local distribution companies — Easton Utilities

Commission and Chesapeake Utilities Corporation – Delaware Division — executed binding long-

term precedent agreements for service on the new facilities, subscribing to 100 percent of the

Project’s incremental capacity under 20-year terms. These local distribution companies provide

critical service to human needs customers, including residential, hospital, and emergency services

customers, in Delaware and Maryland. The natural gas delivered through the Project’s facilities

will support essential heating, cooking, and other daily energy needs for homes, as well as the

reliable operation of hospitals, emergency response facilities, and other public safety infrastructure

that depends on an uninterrupted supply of natural gas.

       Absent the Project, the participating shippers will be unable to meet the demonstrated

demand growth within their service territories, which has already exceeded the firm capacity

currently available on Eastern Shore’s system. As the only interstate natural gas pipeline serving

the Delmarva Peninsula, Eastern Shore takes seriously its obligation to enhance its system and

service offerings to ensure the continuation of safe, reliable, and adequate natural gas service to

the region. The Project is therefore essential to maintaining and improving the natural gas service

on which the communities of the Delmarva Peninsula depend.
 VI.    LANDOWNER NOTIFICATION

       In accordance with Section 157.6(d) of the Commission’s regulations, Eastern Shore has

included a complete list of affected landowners in Exhibit F-1 as Attachment 1-B to Resource

Report 1. The landowner list is being filed in Volume II as privileged information pursuant to 18

Eastern Shore requests privileged treatment for Volume II and has marked the applicable

documents “CUI//PRIV – Do Not Release.”

VII.   ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT

       The Environmental Report attached hereto as Exhibit F-1 more fully describes the potential

environmental impacts of the Project. The information in Exhibit F-1 has been prepared in

accordance with Part 380 of the Commission’s regulations and FERC’s Guidance Manual for

Environmental Report Preparation and meets the requirements for the Commission to perform its

environmental analysis of the Project. As described in detail in the Environmental Report and

summarized below, the Project has been carefully designed to minimize environmental impacts

and will not result in a significant impact on the quality of the human environment.

       The Project will leverage the existing Eastern Shore pipeline system and require minimal

new permanent right-of-way for construction and operation. The five pipeline loop segments —

the Parkesburg-Daleville Loop, the Tidewater Upgrade Segments 1 and 2, the Harrington Loop,

and the Barksdale Loop — are each collocated within or directly adjacent to Eastern Shore’s

existing pipeline corridor, and the associated aboveground valve facilities and the North

Bridgeville M&R Station are sited on or immediately adjacent to existing Eastern Shore-owned

property and facilities. By siting the Project facilities within or alongside existing infrastructure

corridors, Eastern Shore has substantially reduced the need for new land disturbance and new
 permanent easements. In developing the Project, each pipeline loop was evaluated independently

to account for its unique engineering objectives, surrounding land use, environmental constraints,

and operational considerations. During route development, Eastern Shore considered a variety of

factors, including route length, constructability, existing infrastructure, environmental resources,

right-of-way requirements, impacts to residences and businesses, future development, and

opportunities to parallel existing utility corridors where practicable.        Eastern Shore also

incorporated route refinements throughout development of the Project to address engineering

requirements, environmental considerations, and landowner feedback.

       Construction of the Project will be conducted in accordance with all applicable federal,

state, and local environmental regulations and permit requirements. Eastern Shore will implement

environmental protection measures during construction to minimize temporary impacts to soils,

waterbodies, wetlands, and other sensitive resources. Following construction, all temporarily

disturbed areas will be restored to pre-construction conditions or better, in accordance with

applicable restoration standards. Eastern Shore will also comply with the Commission’s Upland

Erosion Control, Revegetation, and Maintenance Plan and its Wetland and Waterbody

Construction and Mitigation Procedures to ensure that construction and restoration activities

adhere to the Commission’s environmental standards.

VIII. RATES AND TARIFF

       Exhibit N establishes the incremental recourse rates that will serve as the applicable cost-

based recourse rate alternative for the Project. The incremental recourse rates are reflected in the

pro forma tariff records included in Exhibit P. The two Project shippers have elected to pay

negotiated rates for firm transportation service on the Project In compliance with Commission

policy, Eastern Shore will file tariff records reflecting its negotiated rate agreements with the
 Project shippers within 30 to 60 days prior to when the underlying negotiated rates are proposed

to become effective. 13
